subject: Hypertide unit economics & next experiments
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Hypertide unit economics & next experiments

Hi Anita / Hypertide team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to hear about the low-latency inference use case and the 20M monthly active requests you're projecting for Q1. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- What we heard: majority of traffic is short-generation (<=128 tokens) for real-time personalization; bursty at 10x peak during campaigns. Primary constraints are per-call latency (<=120ms p95) and predictable cost per 1M tokens.
- Hyperscaler comparison notes: you mentioned a hyperscaler quote that looks cheaper at list price but has higher per-request tail latency and no easy KV caching for repeated user prefixes.

Proposed experiments (small, measurable):
1) 100k-token simulation run comparing Redwood hosted vs Hyperscaler API at your observed token/burst shape (we'll provide a traffic generator).
2) Run with two configs for Redwood: (a) batching optimized for 128-token median, (b) batching disabled with aggressive KV cache warmup to quantify cache-hit delta.
3) Measure: per-1M-token cost estimate, p50/p95 latency, and cache hit rate.

Deliverables from our side: an xlsx with predicted unit costs and a mutual action plan (attached). Can we lock these on Tuesday for an A/B test early next week? If Procurement needs a SOW/PO template, loop them in and Ben will handle pricing.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscale-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet with test matrices), hypertide-mutual-action-plan.pdf (MVP milestone and timelines).

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Grace — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items so we scope the tests correctly: 

- Volume: the 20M/month is our Q1 goal; current pilot is ~1.1M/month. For the bench run, can you simulate both 1M and scaled 10M patterns? We want to see linearity.
- Cache behavior: our personalization layer results in ~30% repeat prefixes today; if Redwood's prefix/KV caching can push that to 60% that's a big win for us.
- Cost sensitivity: at scale our procurement threshold is $X per 1M tokens (an internal target). We won't share exact numbers in email — procurement will handle the formal numbers.

Two quick asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a brief one-pager comparing failure/fallback behavior vs the Hyperscaler if the primary GPU pool is saturated?
2) Can we get an estimated lead time for Private/VPC deployment (we may need it for compliance later)?

I'll loop Procurement after we see the initial test results. Proposed: run the 1M token sim this week, then the scaled 10M next week.

—Anita
Anita Shah

Sounds good — thanks Anita. Quick answers inline and next-week plan: 

- 1M + 10M sims: yes, we can run both. We'll include the same burst profile you shared (10x campaign spikes) and produce tokenized traffic traces you can sanity-check.
- Failure/fallback one-pager: noted — Ben will draft a short doc showing routing fallback to a lower-cost model variant and a cross-region failover pattern.
- Private/VPC lead time: typical onboarding is 4–6 weeks for VPC with standard KMS integration; on-prem varies (we'll provide an estimate).

Next steps:
1) I'll schedule the 1M sim for Thu 9/23 09:00 PT — can you confirm an ops contact to receive the generator credentials?
2) Ben will attach preliminary pricing options (commit tiers + burst).
3) Marissa will propose what cache-hit instrumentation to add so we can measure warm/steady hit rates.

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and drop the Drive link with scripts.

Best,
Grace

Hi all — technical test plan details below (summary):

1) Traffic shapes: we'll run two traces (pilot-shape = 1.1M/mo; target-shape = 10M/mo). Each trace will simulate median=64 tokens, p95=128 tokens. Burst factor = 10x for campaign windows.
2) Configs to compare:
   - Redwood A: latency-optimized batching (max batch 32, dynamic batch window 10ms), KV cache disabled.
   - Redwood B: cost-optimized (batch max 128, 40ms window) + KV prefix cache; measure cold vs warm cache.
   - Hyperscaler: mimic API call pattern with no server-side KV cache (we'll run equivalent batch sizes client-side to keep parity).
3) Metrics: per-1M tokens cost estimate (token accounting + infra amort), p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, and percentage of requests that would hit the lower-cost fallback model.
4) Instrumentation: please add headers to requests: X-Test-Run-ID, X-User-Prefix-Hash so we can correlate cache hits. We'll share the exact schema in the Drive folder.

I uploaded the generator and a sample results template to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-hypertide-tests (link in metadata).

If Procurement needs a line item we can produce a tight 1–page pricing appendix after the 1M run.

—Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
